description: Global regulatory database of banned, restricted, and high-risk food, cosmetic, and packaging substances across major international jurisdictions.

substances.description: White pigment and opacifying agent used in candies, confectionery, chewing gum, pastries, sauces, and white powders.
substances.indian_status_note: Permitted in India under FSSAI Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations 2011 with GMP limits.

bans.regulatory_agency: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) / European Commission
bans.reason_summary: EFSA concluded Titanium Dioxide particles can accumulate in the body and induce DNA strand breaks and chromosomal damage; safe level of daily intake cannot be established.

bans.country_name: United Kingdom (Northern Ireland) & Great Britain Review
bans.legal_citation: Retained EU Regulation 2022/63 (NI) and UK FSA Safety Opinion
bans.reason_summary: Banned in Northern Ireland under EU Protocol; UK FSA and Scottish Food Standards advisory committees recommend phase-out due to lack of established safe limit for DNA toxicity.

bans.regulatory_agency: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO)
bans.reason_summary: Harmonized with EU ban prohibiting E171 in all foodstuffs.

substances.description: Flour improver and dough conditioner used to strengthen bread dough and enable higher rising.
substances.indian_status_note: Banned in India by FSSAI in June 2016 following CSE study showing presence of carcinogens in 84% of Delhi bread samples.

bans.reason_summary: Recognized as a genotoxic renal carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC). Toxic to kidneys and thyroid.
Classified as hazardous to human health with proven carcinogenic potential in laboratory studies.
Removed from approved flour treatment agents list due to demonstrated tumor growth in animals.
Complete prohibition in flour production and bakery operations.

substances.description: Emulsifier and density balancer used in fruit-flavored beverages and citrus sodas to keep flavoring oils suspended.
substances.indian_status_note: Banned in India by FSSAI under the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations 2011.

bans.health_concern: Thyroid toxicity and bioaccumulation of bromine
bans.reason_summary: Bromine accumulates in adipose tissue; linked to neurological impairment, thyroid organ dysfunction, and cardiac lesions.
FDA revoked authorization for use of BVO in food based on animal toxicology studies showing bioaccumulation and toxic thyroid effects.
Prohibited as a food ingredient due to systemic accumulation risks.

bans.regulatory_agency: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
bans.reason_summary: Not on the positive list of authorized food additives in Japan.

substances.description: Chemical blowing agent used in yoga mats, shoe soles, and synthetic leather; also used as a dough conditioner and flour bleaching agent in industrial bakeries.
substances.indian_status_note: Permitted in India in bread manufacturing up to 45 ppm under FSSAI regulations.

bans.health_concern: Respiratory sensitization and semicarbazide (SEM) carcinogen breakdown
bans.reason_summary: Thermal breakdown produces semicarbazide, a known mutagen and animal carcinogen. Linked to asthma and allergic skin reactions in workers.
Prohibited as a flour bleaching agent and dough conditioner.

bans.legal_citation: Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code
bans.reason_summary: Not permitted for use as a food additive in Australia or New Zealand.

bans.health_concern: Severe penalty (up to 15 years imprisonment & $450,000 fine)
bans.reason_summary: Strictly illegal to use ADA in food manufacturing.

substances.canonical_name: Sudan Industrial Dyes (Sudan I, II, III, IV & Para Red)
substances.description: Synthetic industrial azo dyes used to color waxes, oils, and shoe polish; illegally added to chili powder, paprika, curry powders, and palm oil to impart intense red-orange hue.
substances.indian_status_note: Strictly prohibited in all foodstuffs by FSSAI and Indian Spices Board. Spices exported from India are subject to mandatory pre-shipment testing.

bans.regulatory_agency: EFSA / RASFF (Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed)
bans.reason_summary: Azo dyes metabolize in the human body into carcinogenic aromatic amines (such as aniline and o-toluidine); zero tolerance in food products.

bans.health_concern: DNA damage and bladder cancer risk
bans.reason_summary: Illegal in any foodstuff; immediate import refusal and border detention on detection.
Zero tolerance; resulted in the largest food recall in UK history in 2005 (over 600 food products recalled).

substances.canonical_name: Southampton Six Azo Colors (Tartrazine, Allura Red, Sunset Yellow, etc.)
substances.description: Synthetic artificial food dyes used across snacks, carbonated drinks, jams, and confections.
substances.indian_status_note: Permitted in India up to 100 ppm in designated food categories with mandatory 'Contains Permitted Synthetic Food Colour' label.

bans.health_concern: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children
bans.reason_summary: Mandatory warning statement required on packaging: '[Name of color]: may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children.' Led to near-universal phase-out by EU manufacturers.
Mandatory warning label required; FSA actively encourages voluntary removal from food products.
Historically banned outright; harmonized with EU regulations with severe restriction.

substances.description: Preservatives used in personal care lotions, face washes, cosmetics, and creams to prevent microbial growth.
substances.indian_status_note: Permitted under IS 4707 (Part 2) cosmetics standards in India.

bans.regulatory_agency: Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety (SCCS) / European Commission
bans.reason_summary: Exhibits estrogenic activity, interfering with reproductive hormonal regulation; completely prohibited in cosmetic formulations across the EU.
Prohibited in leave-on and rinse-off cosmetic preparations.

substances.description: Fluorinated chemicals applied to fast-food wrappers, pizza boxes, microwave popcorn bags, and paperboard takeout containers for oil and water resistance.
substances.indian_status_note: FSSAI (Packaging) Regulations 2018 do not currently set explicit zero-PFAS thresholds on paperboard.

bans.health_concern: Kidney and testicular cancer, liver toxicity, immune suppression
bans.reason_summary: First country in the world to ban all organic fluorinated compounds in paper and cardboard food contact materials.

bans.legal_citation: FDA Market Phaseout (Feb 2024) & California Health and Safety Code Section 109000
bans.reason_summary: FDA confirmed grease-proofing materials containing PFAS are no longer sold for food contact in the US; California AB 1200 banned PFAS in food packaging from January 2023.

bans.legal_citation: REACH Annex XVII & upcoming universal PFAS restriction
bans.health_concern: Persistence in environment and human blood
bans.reason_summary: Phase-out of all non-essential uses of PFAS under the EU Green Deal Chemicals Strategy.

substances.description: Synthetic growth hormone injected into dairy cows to artificially elevate milk production.
substances.indian_status_note: Banned in India under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act (import and manufacture prohibited).

bans.health_concern: Elevated IGF-1 (linked to prostate and breast cancers), animal welfare (mastitis)
bans.reason_summary: Strict prohibition on marketing and administration of bovine somatotrophin in the EU.

bans.health_concern: Animal health risks and antibiotic residue concerns
bans.reason_summary: Denied regulatory approval due to veterinary health concerns and elevated somatic cell counts in dairy.

bans.regulatory_agency: Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority (APVMA)
bans.legal_citation: Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals Code Act 1994
bans.health_concern: Veterinary welfare and human health risks
bans.reason_summary: Registration not approved for dairy cattle treatment.

substances.description: Synthetic fat substitute used in zero-fat potato chips and savory snacks that cannot be absorbed by the digestive system.
substances.indian_status_note: Not approved by FSSAI on the positive list of authorized food additives.

bans.health_concern: Depletion of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), carotenoid malabsorption, severe gastrointestinal cramps
bans.reason_summary: Denied novel food authorization because it binds to fat-soluble nutrients and carries severe digestive distress risks.
Not approved for use in Canadian foods.
Not approved on the UK permitted food additives list.

substances.description: Artificial non-caloric sweetener 30-50 times sweeter than sucrose, commonly blended with saccharin in diet drinks and confectionery.
substances.indian_status_note: Not permitted in India by FSSAI under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations 2011.

bans.health_concern: Bladder cancer and testicular atrophy in animal models
bans.reason_summary: FDA banned cyclamate in 1969 after laboratory rat studies demonstrated increased bladder tumors when fed cyclamate-saccharin mixtures.
